cands.bio: Attorney and Democrat who has represented San Diego-area California districts in the U.S. House since 2013. Earlier served on the San Diego City Council (1993–2000), the California State Assembly (2000–2006) and the State Senate (2010–2013). Studied at the University of San Diego, Fordham and Harvard Law.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Vargas on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land-use limits, gun laws, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. His stated views on abortion come only from a secondary summary, not from a statement or questionnaire of his own. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so there is no self-reported platform beyond his campaign website. We found no controversy reporting that we could read in full. Ballotpedia's page was cut off partway through the key-votes list. The 2012 and 2006 campaign-era details on his Wikipedia page are not backed by news articles we could open, so we left them out.

cands.name: Jeff Belle

money.note: Individuals gave $19,538; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 52nd Congressional District in 2026. Served in the U.S. Navy from 1978 to 1980. Works as a consultant. Holds a bachelor's degree from Oklahoma City University (2019) and a graduate degree from American Public University System (2021).

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations for Belle from April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn. These are voter guides and media programs, not organizational endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Belle was born or raised, or when he moved to California. We found no record of any elected or appointed office, and his survey's mention of 'federal experience and local experience' is not explained. We found no bills, official actions or filings by Belle, so the positions listed come only from his own statements. We found nothing on his positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, policing, gun laws or abortion. His claim to have 'passed legislation' on housing investors is not backed by any named bill. We found no news coverage of controversies and no foreign ties. Only one page, his Ballotpedia profile, was available for this research.

land-for-floridians.evidence: In his Ballotpedia survey, Belle said he 'passed legislation to prohibit major corporations, private equity firms and China from investing in housing.' The source names no bill or office, so this is recorded as his statement, not a verified deed.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Belle said he supports pro-housing supply, deregulation and tax restraint 'over increasing taxes or restricting development,' and supports streamlined permitting and less regulation.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Belle listed support for 'Special Needs Children School Choice' among his policy priorities.
